Noah L.: quick question — flew home last night and my flight got moved up so i needed to add an extra hotel night the night before. booking was nonrefundable and cost $185. Can i expense it?
Sam (People Ops): short answer: maybe. we generally cover additional nights that are business-required (e.g., early customer meeting or schedule change) but personal preference nights are not reimbursable. :memo:
Noah L.: this was a schedule change from the airline  they pushed my depart earlier and i couldn't get on an earlier flight without missing meetings.
TravelTeamBot: note: if Travel Desk can rebook or cancel and recover funds, they'll try. If you booked independently and it's nonrefundable, submit a preapproval request.
Noah L.: how do i request preapproval retroactively? i didn't have time before booking.
Sam (People Ops): for emergency retroactive approvals we need: 1) manager note approving the emergency change, 2) flight confirmation showing the change (email from airline/agc), and 3) original and changed itineraries/screenshots of the nonrefundable charge. Email people-ops@redwood.com with subject "Retro hotel reimbursement request - [Name] [dates]" and cc your manager. We'll review within 3 business days. Do not assume approval until you get the email.
Noah L.: ok got it. what about corporate card vs personal card? i used my personal card to avoid missing the flight.
Sam (People Ops): personal card is fine for retro bookings. if Travel Desk could have done it on the corporate card but you booked yourself last-minute, we'll still consider reimbursement if the reason was urgent and you followed up with travel to see if they could assist. include that convo in your email.
Finance: finance note: submit the full itemized folio showing payment, the airline change notice, manager approval, and the people-ops preapproval email if granted. Expense category: "Lodging - Emergency/Change". For reimbursements to a non-US vendor, include proof of payment and currency.
Noah L.: any cap on reimbursement for emergency nights?
Sam (People Ops): no fixed cap, but reviewers evaluate reasonableness relative to city rates. if the nightly rate is far above typical for the area we may ask you to provide an alternative or justification.
Noah L.: what if i could've stayed with family but chose hotel to avoid long commute?
Sam (People Ops): then it's personal and won't be reimbursed. we only cover when travel timing or safety/feasibility makes the stay business-required.
TravelTeamBot: tip: when you see potential schedule risk, open a Travel Desk ticket immediately. they can place a soft hold or advise lower-cost alternatives.
Noah L.: thanks  i'll send the email and cc Jordan. appreciated.
